Hi James —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward an Order Form for the pilot, legal asked we run one quick alignment on the Term section so procurement can lock the PO. Two items Acme raised in the procurement call: auto-renew timing and whether the Order Form should include a termination-for-convenience (TfC) right.

To keep momentum, we propose the following compromise so both sides have clarity:
- Mutual TfC allowed after initial 12-month commitment with a 60-day written notice;
- If TfC is exercised, Redwood will provide a 90-day knowledge-transfer/migration support window (scope in attached SOW table);
- Auto-renew will require a written notice to opt-out at least 30 days before renewal date (i.e., client must notify 30 days prior to avoid renewal).

Attaching the current Order Form redline and a short note from legal (suggested wording for Section 9). Can you confirm Acme’s appetite for the compromise above? If yes, we’ll ask Mina to draft the exact language for the MSA/Order Form and route for e-sign.

Team —

I reviewed James’s attachment and the redlines. Proposed legal position that balances risk and sale velocity:

1) Term & Auto-Renew
- Definition: Term = Initial Term (12 months) plus any Renewal Terms.
- Auto-Renew Opt-Out: Customer must notify Redwood in writing at least thirty (30) days prior to expiration of the then-current term for standard Order Forms (initial term >= 12 months). For Pilot Order Forms (initial term < 12 months), Customer must notify Redwood at least fifteen (15) days prior to expiration to avoid renewal.

2) Termination for Convenience (TfC)
- Mutual TfC: Either party may terminate the Order Form for convenience following the Initial Term upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice.
- Winddown Support: Upon TfC, Redwood will provide ninety (90) days of commercially reasonable transition assistance per the SOW. Transition assistance will be subject to a cap of one hundred twenty (120) Professional Services hours unless otherwise agreed in writing; additional hours billed at standard PS rates.

3) Redlines to include: a short schedule describing milestones (knowledge transfer, export of keys/data, access handoff) and a simple PS hour table (cap, rate). We should keep liability carveouts as redlineable but avoid wholesale changes; push back if customer requests extended indemnities tied to TfC.

I’ll draft concrete contract language and a SOW appendix today and attach. If commercial OKs the 120-hour cap, we can send a single redline bundle to Acme and include a DocuSign link.

Mina Haddad
